sourceLesson: Backend LLD: Design Patterns: Decorator and Flyweight

questions.title: Homework Question-01
questions.question: A junior developer says: “I added a wrapper class in front of our payment code, so I’ve used the Facade pattern.” Looking closer, the wrapper only calls into a single third-party payment class, translating its method names and parameter shapes to match what the rest of the codebase expects — no other subsystem is involved. What's the more accurate assessment?

options.optionText: This is actually Adapter, not Facade — it’s translating one incompatible interface, not simplifying coordination across multiple subsystems
This is correctly a Facade, since any wrapper class counts as one
This is neither pattern, since only one class is involved
This is both patterns simultaneously, since it wraps something

questions.title: Python Homework- Scenario Based
questions.question: Your app needs to support OpenAI, Anthropic, and Gemini LLM SDKs, each with different request shapes and parameter names. You want your app to code against one common interface. Which pattern applies, and why?

options.optionText: Facade — because it hides complexity
Adapter — because it translates each SDK’s different shape into one common interface (ChatModel) your app depends on
Singleton — because you only need one instance
Strategy — because you’re switching algorithms

questions.title: Question-05 Python Scenario Based
questions.question: An AI coding assistant receives one user message, then internally pulls context, plans steps, calls tools, updates memory, and returns one final answer. The user sees only “message in, answer out.” What pattern does this AgentFacade.run() represent, and why?

options.optionText: Facade — because it hides the coordination of multiple internal subsystems (retriever, planner, tool executor, memory) behind one simple run() entry point
Adapter — because it translates between different tool APIs
Singleton — because there is only one agent
Builder — because it constructs a response step by step

options.optionText: Single Responsibility — PhonePe should not have a constructor
Dependency Injection — bank_api should never be passed into init

questions.title: Question - 08 scenario based Intermediate
questions.question: A ride-hailing app needs to: (1) call three different maps SDKs — Google Maps, Mapbox, and OpenStreetMap — through one common MapProvider interface, and (2) offer callers a single book_ride() method that internally picks a map provider, calculates fare, finds a driver, and sends a confirmation. Which combination of patterns fits, and how would they relate to each other?

options.optionText: Only one Facade is needed — it can also handle translating the three different maps SDKs internally
One Adapter per maps SDK (to normalize their different APIs into MapProvider), plus one Facade around book_ride() that uses those adapters as part of its coordination
Only three Adapters are needed — book_ride() doesn't need a Facade since it's just one method
This scenario doesn't fit either pattern since it involves both APIs and multi-step coordination

questions.title: Adapter & Facade Question-1
questions.question: A Builder class controls the step-by-step construction of a complex object. An Adapter class wraps an existing object so a client can call it through a different interface. Both classes "wrap" something in some sense. Why is Builder a Creational pattern while Adapter is a Structural pattern?

options.optionText: Builder is concerned with assembling an object into existence; Adapter is concerned with connecting an already-existing object to a client that can’t call it directly
Builder uses inheritance while Adapter uses composition
Builder is used for simple objects and Adapter is used for complex objects
There’s no real difference — the classification is arbitrary

questions.title: Adapter & Facade Scenario Based
questions.question: Your app calls Yes Bank’s do_payment() and get_acc_balance() directly everywhere in the codebase. Business now wants to add HDFC Bank, whose method names are totally different. What’s the correct fix per the lecture?

options.optionText: Edit Yes Bank’s source code so its method names match HDFC’s
Create a common BankAPI interface, and write one adapter class per bank that translates calls into that bank’s real methods
Rewrite PhonePe with if/elif branches for each bank
Merge Yes Bank and HDFC into a single class

questions.title: Python - Debug the code
questions.question:
```python
class Amazon:
    def order_place(self):
        self.invoice_generation()
        self.wms.update()
        self.ims.update()
        self.emails.send_email()
```

The team wants to apply the Facade pattern here to keep Amazon clean. What's wrong with the current code from a Facade perspective?

options.optionText: The method name `order_place` should be renamed to `facade_order_place`
Amazon is missing a BankAPI interface
There's nothing wrong — this already is a Facade
Amazon.order_place() is doing the coordination job of four unrelated subsystems itself, instead of delegating to a dedicated Facade class

questions.title: Python- scenario based
questions.question: A class talks to three different logging services, each with a different API, and combines their output into one log() method. According to the lecture, this design is:

options.optionText: Both — one Adapter per logging service to normalize each API, all sitting inside one Facade that exposes a single log() method
Only an Adapter, since it's about translating between APIs
Only a Facade, since it exposes one simple method
Neither — this is a Factory pattern

questions.title: Debug the code - Intermediate Question-6

options.optionText: It's missing a try/except block around pay()
It re-introduces the exact bank-selection coupling the Adapter pattern was meant to eliminate — adding a new bank still means editing this class
PhonePeFacade should inherit from BankAPI
The constructor should not take phone_pe as a parameter

questions.title: Thoery for Beginner Question-07
questions.question: Suppose PhonePe is later refactored so it depends directly on YesBankAdapter (not on the BankAPI interface). It still works fine today. What has actually been lost by removing the interface, even though nothing is broken yet?

options.optionText: Nothing — as long as it compiles and passes tests, the interface was optional
The ability to swap in a different adapter (e.g., for HDFC) without changing PhonePe’s code — PhonePe is now coupled to one specific adapter class instead of an abstraction
YesBankAdapter would stop being able to wrap YesBank
The Adaptee (YesBank) would need to change its method names
